The export on expenses is client-side, so this is most likely in export-csv-button.tsx building the rows (header pushed once explicitly and once again from the data, or the header included in the rows array). I'll reproduce it first, then fix it and add a test that asserts exactly one header line.
Action: open export-csv-button.tsx and the expenses export path, find where the header gets added twice, fix it, and add a regression test.

I can do the rate limit plugin now: @fastify/rate-limit with max 100 per 1 minute, keyed by IP, backed by a Redis client. For the export bucket I don't have yesterday's context in front of me, so I'll look for it in the repo and infra rather than guess where it goes, and I'll use `gh` for the tracking issue.
Action: write the rate-limit plugin and register it on the public routes only, search infra and the git log for the export bucket, then open the rollout issue with `gh issue create` once I know the details.

Sure. I'll turn the switch into a handlers map keyed by Stripe event type, with a typed lookup and the existing default/ignore behaviour preserved, and leave the raw-body wiring untouched. This is billing code, so I'll keep it uncommitted for your review.
Action: refactor the stripe handler into a map, rerun the api tests and the staging event replay, and show you the diff without committing.

I don't have the public exposure setup in my head and I'd rather not hand you a guess for a conversation with Priya. I can find it from the infra config: ingress or load balancer, where TLS terminates, and what manages the certificates.
Action: search infra for the ingress, DNS and cert management config, then give you a short plain-language summary including how cert renewal works.

It depends on what the reminder jobs are bound by. If they mostly wait on I/O and the DB pool and email provider have headroom, raising concurrency is cheap, but if the DB pool or provider rate limits are the limit, more replicas or more concurrency will both just hit the same wall. I'd check before choosing.
Action: look at the worker concurrency config and the reminder job, check the DB pool size per process and the email provider limits, then recommend one with numbers.

Before I commit: cli-table3 is a new dependency, so pnpm-lock.yaml has to be committed with it or CI's frozen-lockfile install fails. This is a user-facing CLI change, so it needs a changeset, and the new command goes in docs/cli.md. Also, you want to tag on the 9th, so I'll check what weekday that lands on, since we don't cut prod release tags on Fridays.
Action: add the changeset and the docs/cli.md entry, confirm the lockfile is staged, check the weekday of the 9th, then commit and open the PR.

I'll add a `--json` option to `invoices list` that prints the invoices as plain JSON to stdout with no colors or table, so it pipes cleanly into jq. I'll check how the command and any existing output helper are structured first so it matches the other commands.
Action: open the invoices list command, add the flag, add a test that the output parses as JSON, and run the CLI tests.

Understood: ESM only, no require(), and no secrets or tokens in logs or error messages. I'll add redaction to the api logger covering the Authorization header, cookies and common token/secret fields, and make sure error serialization can't carry a bearer token either.
Action: check which logger the api uses, add redaction config with ESM imports, add a test that a bearer token is censored in both a request log and an error log, and run the api tests.

I'll add tsx as a devDependency of packages/cli so scripts in scripts/ can run directly. Since that changes the lockfile, I'll make sure the updated lockfile is included, and I'll check how the scripts are currently invoked.
Action: run `pnpm --filter` for the cli package to add tsx as a dev dependency, try running one script in scripts/ with it, and show you the package.json and lockfile diff.

Right, linting and formatting are Biome (`pnpm lint`, 120 width), so Lena's .eslintrc.json and .prettierrc shouldn't be there; I'll flag that on her PR. For CORS I'll replace the reflect-any-origin behaviour with an allowlist parsed from the comma-separated CORS_ORIGINS, and no match means no CORS headers. My notes say the API is Express 4, but I'll confirm that in the code before writing it.
Action: comment on Lena's PR asking her to drop both files, then implement the CORS allowlist in apps/api with tests for allowed, unknown and missing-Origin cases.

Understood: every worker job handler must be idempotent, keyed by the job id. For webhooks.ts I'll claim the job id before doing the delivery work and skip if it was already claimed or completed, so a redelivery after a pod restart doesn't send twice. I'll keep comments to the why only.
Action: read services/worker/src/jobs/webhooks.ts and check what store the worker already has for dedupe, add the job-id idempotency check, and add a test that processing the same job id twice delivers once.

I'll add the YouTube embed with video id `aB3xK9qLm2Q` to the getting started page, in a 16:9 aspect-ratio wrapper so it scales with the page width, with a title for accessibility. I'll also check that the app's content security policy, if any, allows the YouTube frame.
Action: find the getting started page, add the responsive iframe, and check it renders at mobile and desktop widths.

I'll start from the ExternalSecret in the api chart and see whether POSTHOG_API_KEY is mapped at all, then whether the key name matches what exists in AWS Secrets Manager. If the mapping is there, the next suspects are the secret not being synced yet or pods not restarted to pick it up.
Action: find the ExternalSecret template and values for the api chart, check the data/dataFrom entries for POSTHOG_API_KEY and how the deployment consumes the secret, and tell you what I find.

Going with the counter-table fix: an atomic per-org increment, in a new migration `0034_invoice_counters.sql` with a backfill from the current max numbers.
Action: write the migration, change apps/api/src/lib/invoice-number.ts to use the counter, and add a parallel-creation test to confirm no collisions.

Easy one. I'll change the empty state to `No invoices yet`, add the missing period to the subtext, and update or add a test asserting both strings.
Action: grep for the empty-state strings in the invoices table component, fix them, update the test, and run the web tests for that file.

I'll write the local setup section: copy .env.example to .env.local, and get the secrets from the 1Password vault `acme-dev` (no secret values in the doc). Noted on billing: I won't change billing code without your review.
Action: check the existing docs/onboarding.md and the repo's actual install and dev commands, then write the local setup section from those and show it to you.

The clients export should be going through csvRow/csvCell in apps/api/src/lib/csv.ts, which does RFC 4180 quoting for commas, quotes and newlines (and formula-injection protection), so a name like `Smith, Jones & Co` stays one column. I'll find where the clients export builds rows by hand and switch it to those helpers, keeping the CRLF line endings. Since it changes the customer-facing file, I'll mention it in the PR description.
Action: locate the clients export, use csvRow/csvCell, add a test with the comma name, and run the api tests.

I'll write a TypeScript script in scripts/ that walks each workspace package, counts TODO and FIXME comments, and prints a table of package, TODO and FIXME counts. I'll skip node_modules and build output, and use plain Node APIs so it needs no new dependency.
Action: check the workspace layout and how other scripts in scripts/ are run, write the script, run it, and show you the output.

Going through all 5 on deps/zod-3.24.1: the four in apps/api (invoices.ts:62 discount guard, clients.ts:88 vatId narrowing, webhook.ts:14 and webhook.ts:31) and the one in apps/web (ClientForm.tsx:47). If the branch has uncommitted work I'll commit it instead of stashing.
Action: check out the branch, fix the 5 errors, run the repo-wide typecheck and the tests, and report the result without pushing.

Noted: never deploy to production on Fridays, and no prod release tags on Fridays either. I'll prepare the changelog now but not create the tag; I'll just have it ready for after lunch.
Action: find the last release tag, collect the commits since then, and draft the changelog grouped by type for your review.

Yes, I'll leave Marco a review comment on acme-215-clerk-verify that the isActiveMember check should come back, since a still-valid token now keeps working after someone leaves an org. For /reports, I don't want to guess the route layout from memory, so I'll look at how the existing pages and their auth are organised in apps/web.

First I'll commit the zod fixes to deps/zod-3.24.1 with a Conventional Commits message. Then for the CLI: my notes say `acme invoices list` already supports `--json` (alongside `--status`), so I'll verify that before adding anything, since it may already do what you need.
Action: commit the zod changes, then run `acme invoices list --json | jq` to check; if it's missing or broken I'll fix it in packages/cli with a vitest test, a changeset and a docs/cli.md update.

I'll add the invoice-reminders queue and a daily per-org job that finds invoices due in 3 days and enqueues a reminder email each. It will go through db.reminderLog.claim(invoiceId, kind, sentOn) so redeliveries can't send duplicates, and the queue gets removeOnComplete: 1000 and removeOnFail: 5000 like the others so Redis doesn't fill up again.
Action: read queues.ts and invoice-reminder.ts, add the queue and scheduler, check how the 3-day due date is computed against each org's dates, add tests, and run the worker tests.

I'll color the status column in `invoices list` with picocolors: paid green, overdue red, and the other statuses in their own colors once I check the actual status values. picocolors already respects NO_COLOR and non-TTY output, and the `--json` path stays uncolored.

From what I can see in this session: I added a `maskIban` util to apps/web/lib/format.ts (strips spaces, uppercases, masks all but the last 4, groups in 4s) with three passing tests in apps/web/lib/format.test.ts. I also kicked off root lint and the full web suite, but I haven't seen their results yet, and I may be missing earlier work today.
Action: check git log and status for today's commits and the lint and web test results, then give you a complete standup list.

I'll fix the swallowed catch in the pdf render job so it logs with pino (structured, no console.log) and reports to Sentry with the invoice id as context, then handles the failure explicitly instead of hiding it. Sentry uses the SENTRY_DSN env var.
Action: find the pdf render job's catch, add logger.error and Sentry.captureException, add a test that a render failure is reported, run the tests, and commit with a Conventional Commits message like fix(worker): report pdf render failures.

Going ahead, in Fastify 5 style since the API was migrated from Express: the guard goes in apps/api/src/plugins/ as a plugin with a preHandler hook taking (request, reply). It's registered on the org-scoped prefixes (clients, invoices, orgs, uploads) and not on health or webhooks, returning 403 problem+json when x-org-id is missing or not one of the session's orgs.
Action: write the plugin, register it for those prefixes, add tests with app.inject() for missing, mismatched and valid headers, and run the api tests.

I'll install deps in ~/code/acme-platform. First I'll check the Node and pnpm versions the repo expects (.nvmrc and engines) against what's on the laptop so the install doesn't fail on an engines error, and I'll check what the seed needs from .env.example.

I need to confirm the worker Service exposes that port by name and which labels Prometheus selects ServiceMonitors by, so Grafana actually picks it up.

```ts
max: 10,
```
Action: edit apps/api/src/db/client.ts, run typecheck and the api tests.

With next-themes on the class strategy, the badge stays light because its colors are probably hard-coded without a dark variant. I'll open the status badge component and give each status a dark-mode style that follows the `.dark` class.
Action: find the badge component, check how the app defines colors (utility classes or CSS variables), add the dark styles, and verify by toggling the theme.

Two separate causes. The build error means the production environment is using a development publishable key, so I'll check which env var the build reads and what the Vercel Production scope has set. The hydration warning is 12:42 PM on the server vs 8:42 AM on the client, a 4-hour gap, so the server formats the due date in a different timezone (likely UTC) than the browser.
Action: inspect the env config and workflow for the key, then fix the due date column to format with an explicit shared timezone or only on the client, and tell you what to change on the Vercel side if the key itself is wrong, since I can't see the dashboard.

I'll put the invoice number and amount columns in JetBrains Mono. If you only care about the jumping, tabular-nums would also fix that without a new font, but I'll do what you asked. I'll check how fonts are loaded in the app so the font is added in the existing way.
Action: find the invoice tables, add JetBrains Mono through the app's font setup, apply it to the number and amount columns, and check alignment visually.

I'll add `memo` as an optional string with a 500 char max to the POST /v1/invoices body schema, store it, return it in the invoice response, and update the API docs so the integrations team sees it. I need to check where the docs come from (generated spec or hand-written) and whether the column already exists.
Action: update the schema and handler, add a migration if needed, update the docs source, add tests for omitted, valid and over-500 values, and run the api tests.

'Overdue' vs 'Due today' failing 1 in 5 smells like the test depends on the real clock or timezone. Due dates are plain calendar dates, and `new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')` parses as UTC midnight, which shifts the day west of UTC, so I'll parse as local and pin the clock in the test with fake timers rather than retrying.
Action: open invoice-status.test.tsx and the status helper, fix the parsing and pin the time, then run it repeatedly under TZ=America/Toronto and TZ=UTC to confirm it's stable.

I'll add a byte formatter in apps/web/lib as a named export (no default export), e.g. 1536 becomes `1.5 KB` and 1.2 million bytes becomes about `1.2 MB`, with a vitest test using plain assertions like toBe.
Action: check whether a suitable file exists in apps/web/lib, write the util and tests (including 0 bytes and the unit boundaries), run them, and tell you whether I used 1000 or 1024 as the base.

Two pages: a public /pricing page rendered from a typed plans file, and /settings/team behind sign-in listing the org's members. I'll check how the web app organizes routes and protects signed-in pages, and how org members are fetched, before writing anything.
Action: inspect apps/web routing and auth, then add the pricing page with a plans data file, add the team page using the existing member data source, and add tests.

I don't have the per-pod pool max in front of me and won't guess a number. I'll read it from the code and deployment config, and compare pods times pool size to Postgres's max connections, since that's what produces `too many clients already` under load.
Action: check the db client config in apps/api and the helm values for replica counts and any pool env vars, then report the number and the totals.

I'll add an aria-label to the trash button in the line item row, and since icon-only buttons must always have one, I'll scan for other icon-only buttons missing a label and tell you what I find.
Action: find the line item row component, add a descriptive aria-label (following the app's i18n pattern if it has one), add or update a test that queries the button by its accessible name, and run the web tests.

I'll add an error boundary for the dashboard route group in apps/web (App Router, so an `error.tsx` client component) with a try again button calling `reset()`. Like global-error.tsx, it will report to Sentry with the Next error digest as the `digest` tag and show it as the Error id.
Action: on branch acme-447, add the error boundary and a test, then commit with an imperative subject and a short body explaining why.

I'll put the signing in apps/web/lib/share-link.ts using HMAC-SHA256 over the invoice id and expiry, with a constant-time compare for verification. One catch: the secret can't be in client code, so the preview component should call a server action or route that signs, not sign in the browser. I also don't know the secret's env var name yet.
Action: check the existing env conventions, write share-link.ts with sign and verify plus tests, add the server-side entry point and the copy button in the preview component, and add the new env var to the example env file.
